findings.evidence: The file opens with `@[expose] public section`; `rank` has constructor simp lemmas, `cartanMatrix` has constructor simp lemmas, and `HasCartanType` has `hasCartanType_iff_reindex`, so exposing their bodies is unnecessary API.
findings.fix: Remove the blanket `@[expose]`; keep bodies opaque and add any constructor or introduction/elimination lemmas needed by consumers.
findings.issue: `@[expose] public section` exposes every definition body, including `rank`, `Valid`, `IsSimplyLaced`, `cartanMatrix`, and `HasCartanType`, making downstream proofs depend on implementation reduction despite the supplied characterization lemmas.

findings.evidence: Grep finds only `valid_A`, `valid_B`, `valid_C`, and `valid_D` at lines 142–145, and no constructor lemmas for `IsSimplyLaced` defined at line 159.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` lemmas for every constructor of both predicates (or equivalent exhaustive characteristic iff lemmas), then keep the definitions opaque.
findings.issue: `Valid` and `IsSimplyLaced` lack complete constructor-level simp APIs: `Valid` has lemmas only for `A`–`D`, while `IsSimplyLaced` has none, so users must unfold the predicates to reduce exceptional or simply-laced cases.

summary: The public surface exposes implementation bodies globally and leaves the predicate APIs incomplete without unfolding them.
